title: P02/P45-family handoff, exact version of 072: halve every residual-stream write and quarter every LayerNorm eps after pretraining (bit-exact function-preserving rescale)
description: P02 follow-up in the P45/P46 handoff family (no backlog ID matches exactly), on the Muon incumbent: after the unchanged 070-claude pretraining, multiply emb.weight and every block's proj and fc2 weights and biases by 0.5 and every LayerNorm eps (ln1, ln2, ln_f) by 0.25, which makes the handoff exactly function-preserving (LN(s*x; s^2*eps) = LN(x; eps)) and fixes 072-claude, whose eps-induced logit drift (1.6-2.1) cut round-1 targets to 92/284/102 versus 070's 200/324/206. If the 1x/3x/10x Muon-decay gains (316/327/353) came from smaller weights being more plastic under the frozen RL AdamW, doubling these weights' relative RL step size from an undamaged start should keep 070's round-1 policy and add 072's fast later-round RL gains, raising dev-transfer >=7.
hypothesis: 072-claude's inexact rescale still scored +11/+15 on seeds 0/1 over 070 after a start damaged by LayerNorm-eps drift, and its RL caught up fast (s0 targets 92->273->601->761), which suggests the residual writers' doubled relative RL step size is useful while the damaged start cost seed 2 (-53). With eps also scaled by s^2 the handed-off function is bit-identical (local CPU check on a fork GPT(99,5,256,8) with spread-out embedding row norms: max logit drift exactly 0.0 versus 4.6 for 072's version), so round-1 sampling matches 070 in distribution and any difference comes from the frozen RL AdamW (per-element steps ~lr, wd 0.1 decoupled) moving emb/proj/fc2 twice as far relative to their size. The LayerNorm readers (qkv, fc1, head) and gains are untouched. Mechanism predictions: round-1 targets and sample accuracy within noise of 070 on every seed (no systematic drop as in 072), and RL-solved after round 4 above 070's 788/783/838 on at least 2 of 3 seeds. If plasticity is not the mechanism, this is a no-op; if doubled writer plasticity destabilizes expert iteration, later rounds and dev-transfer fall.
expected_delta: -35 to +35 theorems at >=7 (central guess +5); pretraining identical to 070 (~4750 steps, final val loss 0.091-0.096, held-out greedy ~0.987); logged handoff logit drift < 1e-4 on every seed; round-1 targets within noise of 070's 200/324/206; totals under 1100 s

arch.change: none versus 070-claude during pretraining; at handoff the residual-stream writers are rescaled and every LayerNorm eps is scaled by the square (see handoff); parameter count unchanged
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: GPT(vocab, 5, 256, 8) from the fork, then set every nn.LayerNorm eps to 2.5e-6 (eps is a module attribute, not in the state dict); model.cfg records n_layer=5 and the state dict has blocks.0-blocks.4
arch.kv_cache: one fork KV-cache dict per logical block (5 per sample), unchanged fork code
arch.layernorm_eps: 1e-5 during pretraining; 2.5e-6 (=1e-5*RESID_SCALE^2) on ln1/ln2/ln_f from handoff on

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon on hidden matrices and the output readout head.weight throughout; continuous AdamW auxiliary (unchanged from 069-claude except Muon weight decay)

muon.precision: bf16 Newton-Schulz; fp32 momentum and parameters
muon.shape_scale: sqrt(max(1, rows/columns)) per orthogonalized matrix: Q/K/V each 1, attention output 1, fc1 2, fc2 1, head (99,256) 1
muon.schedule: same warmup/cosine fraction as AdamW; muon_lr = 0.01 * adam_lr / 0.001
muon.parameters: All 20 hidden projection parameters (4 per block x 5 blocks) plus head.weight (99,256; vocab 99, no bias) are in Muon: 21 matrices. Five qkv.weight matrices of shape (768,256) use independent Q/K/V updates, represented as a batch of three (256,256) matrices; proj/fc1/fc2 and head are orthogonalized whole. head is wide (99<256) so it is not transposed and its update has 99 singular values near 1.
muon.license: MIT; full copyright and permission notice retained in pretrain.py
muon.qkv_split: After elementwise Nesterov momentum, reshape each QKV update to (3,256,256); independently Frobenius-normalize and run five batched Newton-Schulz steps; reshape back before applying. No extra learning-rate multiplier. Momentum and weight decay stay elementwise and unchanged.

optimizer.adamw_parameters: emb.weight, all projection biases and LayerNorm parameters (incl. ln_f) throughout; head.weight and hidden matrices never enter pretraining AdamW
optimizer.decay_convention: Unchanged from 070-claude: MUON_WD = 10 * WD * LR / MUON_LR = 0.1 on all 21 Muon matrices (peak per-step shrinkage 1e-3); AdamW auxiliary wd 0.1 at lr 1e-3.
optimizer.clipping: joint global gradient norm 1.0 before both optimizers
optimizer.handoff: CHANGED: after the pretraining loop and model.eval(), under no_grad, multiply by RESID_SCALE=0.5: emb.weight (99x256), and in each of the 5 blocks proj.weight, proj.bias, fc2.weight, fc2.bias (21 tensors). Every residual write is read only through ln1/ln2/ln_f (LayerNorm, eps 1e-5), so logits change only through eps; the max |logit| difference on the first 128 val records (fp32, no autocast) is logged and returned as stats.handoff_logit_drift (local CPU check on a random-init fork GPT(99,5,256,8) with a 10x-scaled embedding: 4.5e-4 at logit scale 1.4). Not rescaled: qkv, fc1, head, LayerNorm gains/biases. Pretraining optimizer states are discarded and the frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW (lr per harness, wd 0.1, betas 0.9/0.95, clip 1.0), whose ~lr-sized per-element steps are then ~2x larger relative to the rescaled weights.

config.init: Exactly 070-claude (= 069-claude): fork default construction with 5 blocks, then orthogonal_ on every 2D block parameter (gain 0.02*sqrt(max(rows, cols))); embedding and readout keep the fork normal(0.02); biases zero. Initial weights and data order/shift RNG streams per seed identical to 070-claude.
config.handoff: CHANGED versus 072: after the pretraining loop and model.eval(), under no_grad, multiply by RESID_SCALE=0.5: emb.weight (99x256), and in each of the 5 blocks proj.weight, proj.bias, fc2.weight, fc2.bias (21 tensors), AND multiply every nn.LayerNorm's eps (5x ln1, 5x ln2, ln_f; 11 modules) by RESID_SCALE^2=0.25, so LN(0.5*x; eps/4) = LN(x; eps) exactly and the handed-off function is unchanged (power-of-two scalings are exact in floating point). Max |logit| difference on the first 128 val records (fp32, no autocast, all positions including pads) is logged and returned as stats.handoff_logit_drift. Not rescaled: qkv, fc1, head, LayerNorm gains/biases. Pretraining optimizer states are discarded and the frozen RL creates its own unchanged AdamW (lr 3e-4, wd 0.1, betas 0.9/0.95, clip 1.0), whose ~lr-sized per-element steps are then ~2x larger relative to the rescaled weights. The KV-cache path is unchanged fork code.
